items.label: Setup S-1
items.nl: A single stationary trajectory of length \(T\) from a time-homogeneous partially observed Markov decision process with binary observed state \(X_t\in\mathcal X=\{0,1\}\), binary hidden state \(H_t\in\mathcal H=\{0,1\}\), joint state \(S_t=(X_t,H_t)\in\mathcal S\), binary action \(A_t\in\mathcal A=\{0,1\}\), and reward \(Y_t\in\mathcal Y=[0,1]\). A joint reward--next-state kernel \(K(dy,s'\mid s,a)\) generates \((Y_t,S_{t+1})\) given the full pre-action history \(\mathcal F_t^-\) and \(A_t\); the known memoryless behavior policy \(b\) draws \(A_t\) given \(X_t\), and \(e\) is the known memoryless target policy. Each policy \(p\in\{b,e\}\) induces a joint-state transition matrix \(P_p\) with stationary law \(d_p\); \(r_e\) is the target-policy mean reward and \(\theta=d_er_e\). Only \(\mathsf O_T=((X_t,A_t,Y_t))_{t=1}^T\) is observed. Regime constants are \(t_0>0\), \(\zeta\geq0\), \(\alpha=e^{-1/t_0}\), \(L=e^{\zeta}\); observable scores are \(\rho_t\), \(Z_t(k)\), with population moments \(m_k\) and empirical moments \(\widehat m_k\), and \(\mathcal M_T^{(2)}(t_0,\zeta)\) is the class of such experiments satisfying the six law conditions.

items.label: Setup S-2
items.nl: Auxiliary finite linear algebra on the four-point joint-state space: row-stochastic \(4\times4\) matrices \(P,P'\) with initial laws \(\nu,\nu'\), reward vectors \(r,r'\in[0,1]^4\), stationary laws \(\pi,\pi'\), transient characteristic polynomials \(q_P(z)=\det(zI-P)/(z-1)\), \(q_{P'}\), pair polynomial \(Q_{P,P'}=q_Pq_{P'}=\sum_{k=0}^6Q_kz^k\), Dobrushin coefficient \(\delta(R)=\max_{i,j}\|R(i,\cdot)-R(j,\cdot)\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\), and stability constant \(B_\alpha=((1+\alpha)/(1-\alpha))^6\).

items.label: Setup S-4
items.nl: The cardinality-uniform bounded-stationary-overlap comparator: stationary-overlap bound \(C>1\), radius \(q_C=(C-1)/C\), exponent \(\beta=2/(2+t_0\zeta)\), and reset-chain depth \(Q\) with hidden alphabet of size \(2(Q+1)\).

items.label: Definition P-1
items.nl: \(\mathcal M_T^{(2)}(t_0,\zeta):=\{(K,b,e,\mathcal L(\mathsf O_T)):T\in\mathbb N,\ \mathcal X=\mathcal H=\mathcal A=\{0,1\},\ \mathcal Y=[0,1],\ \mathrm A_{\mathrm{kernel}},\mathrm A_{\mathrm{ign}},\mathrm A_{\mathrm{start}},\mathrm A_{\mathrm{overlap}},\mathrm A_{b\text{-}\mathrm{mix}},\mathrm A_{e\text{-}\mathrm{mix}}\text{ hold}\}\), where the six predicates are exactly \(\mathrm{ass{:}pomdp\text{-}kernel}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}sequential\text{-}ignorability}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}stationary\text{-}start}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}policy\text{-}overlap}\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}behavior\text{-}contraction}\), and \(\mathrm{ass{:}target\text{-}contraction}\).

items.label: Definition P-2
items.nl: \(\theta(K,e):=d_er_e=\sum_{s=(x,h)\in\mathcal S}d_e(s)\sum_{a\in\mathcal A}e(a\mid x)\sum_{s'\in\mathcal S}\int_{\mathcal Y}yK(dy,s'\mid s,a)\).

items.label: Definition P-4
items.nl:
Let \(M:=\lceil(22+36/\alpha)Tceil\), let \(\mathcal G_M\) be the four-simplex grid with coordinates in \(M^{-1}\mathbb Z\), let \(U:=\mathbf1\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}/4\), and let \(\lambda:=\alpha/(\alpha+6/M)\). Enumerate every \((
u,R,r)\) with \(
u\in\mathcal G_M\), every row of \(R\) in \(\mathcal G_M\), \(\delta(R)\le\alpha+6/M\), and \(r\in\{0,1/M,\ldots,1\}^4\); form \(P=\lambda R+(1-\lambda)U\), select lexicographically among minimizers of \(\max_{0\le k\le6}|\widehat m_k-
u P^kr|\), and output \(\widehat	heta_T:=\pi(P)r\), where \(\pi(P)P=\pi(P)\).

items.label: Definition P-5
items.nl: \(R_T^{(2)}(t_0,\zeta):=\inf_{\widetilde\theta\in\sigma(\mathsf O_T,b,e,t_0,\zeta)}\sup_{M\in\mathcal M_T^{(2)}(t_0,\zeta)}\mathbb E_M[(\widetilde\theta-\theta)^2]\), where the infimum ranges over measurable observed-data procedures taking values in \( [0,1] \).

items.label: Definition P-6
items.nl:
For \(v\in\{-v_T,+v_T\}\), put \(b(1\mid x)=e(1\mid x)=1/2\), let \(E(x\mid h)=3/5\) if \(x=h\) and \(E(x\mid h)=2/5\) otherwise, set \(q_v(h)=1/2+(2h-1)/8+v\), and set \(p(a)=1/4+a/2\).  Define
\[
 K_v^{(T)}(y,x',h'\mid x,h,a)
 :=\operatorname{Ber}_{q_v(h)}(y)\operatorname{Ber}_{p(a)}(h')E(x'\mid h').
\]

items.label: Definition P-7
items.nl: The handle \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{poly}}\) is the problem of constructing, in an explicit arithmetic or bit-complexity and precision model, a cost-certified algorithm that starts from the \(3\times3\) Hankel matrix of differences \(\widehat m_{i+j+1}-\widehat m_{i+j}\), adapts over recurrence ranks zero through three, enforces transient roots in \(\{z:|z|\leq\alpha\}\), and returns a stable four-state scalar realization whose seven-moment objective is globally certified to within \(T^{-1}\) of the optimum, uniformly over rank-deficient strata and without a positive singular-value margin.  The exhaustive estimator is defined over a finite candidate list of size \(O(T^{19})\) for fixed \(t_0\), but no runtime or arithmetic-operation bound for fitting and selection is asserted.

items.label: Definition P-8
items.nl: Can the handle \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{poly}}\) implement fitting and lexicographic selection over, or replace, the \(O(T^{19})\)-sized stable-grid candidate list by a rank-adaptive algorithm with explicit runtime, bit-complexity, and precision semantics that returns over \(\mathcal M_T^{(2)}(t_0,\zeta)\) a globally certified seven-moment stable fit within objective gap \(T^{-1}\), uniformly over every rank-deficient Hankel stratum and without a positive singular-value margin?

items.label: Assumption A-4
items.nl: \(e(a\mid x)\le Lb(a\mid x)\) for every \((a,x)\in\mathcal A\times\mathcal X\).

items.label: Lemma L-1
items.nl:
If \(\delta(P)\le\alpha\) and \(\delta(P')\le\alpha\), then eigenvalue one is algebraically simple for both matrices and \(Q_{P,P'}(1)(\pi r-\pi'r')=\sum_{k=0}^{6}Q_k(
u P^kr-
u'P'^kr')\). Consequently, \( |\pi r-\pi'r'|\le B_\alpha\max_{0\le k\le6}|
u P^kr-
u'P'^kr'|\). The identity holds without diagonalizability and therefore includes repeated, defective, and complex transient modes.

items.label: Lemma L-2
items.nl: For every member of \(\mathcal M_T^{(2)}(t_0,\zeta)\) and every \(k=0,\ldots,6\), the \(k+1\)-action score with \(k\) state transitions satisfies \(m_k=\mathbb E_b[Z_t(k)]=d_bP_e^kr_e\).  Moreover, \(\mathbb E_b[Z_t(k)^2]\leq L^{k+1}\), and, for \(h\geq k+1\), \(\lvert\operatorname{Cov}(Z_t(k),Z_{t+h}(k))\rvert\leq\alpha^{h-k-1}\).

items.label: Lemma L-3
items.nl: For both \(v\in\{-v_T,+v_T\}\), the kernel \(K_v^{(T)}\) and the displayed coincident policies define members of \(\mathcal M_T^{(2)}(t_0,\zeta)\) for every \(t_0>0\), \(\zeta\geq0\), and \(T\geq12\).  Their target values differ by \(1/(8\sqrt T)\), and their observed trajectory laws satisfy \(\operatorname{KL}(\mathbb P_{+}^{\mathsf O_T}\Vert\mathbb P_{-}^{\mathsf O_T})\leq1/12\).  Moreover, \(e=b\) and \(d_e=d_b\), so this pair obeys every stationary occupancy-ratio bound \(d_e\leq Cd_b\) with \(C>1\).

items.label: Theorem T-1
items.nl:
For every fixed \(t_0>0\), \(\zeta\geq0\), and \(T\geq12\), the fully observed-data estimator \(\widehat\theta_T\) satisfies
\[
 \sup_{M\in\mathcal M_T^{(2)}(t_0,\zeta)}
 \mathbb E_M[(\widehat\theta_T-\theta)^2]
 \leq \frac{B_\alpha^2(112V_{\alpha,L}+2)}{T}.
\]
This bound is uniform over zero behavior cells, singular emissions, arbitrarily small stationary cells, and every dependence between reward and next state allowed by \(K\); it requires no stationary occupancy-ratio bound.

items.label: Theorem T-2
items.nl:
For every fixed \(t_0>0\), \(\zeta\geq0\), and \(T\geq12\),
\[
 \frac1{1024T}
 \leq R_T^{(2)}(t_0,\zeta)
 \leq\frac{B_\alpha^2(112V_{\alpha,L}+2)}T.
\]
Thus the exact fixed-binary mean-squared-error rate is \(T^{-1}\), without a stationary occupancy-ratio assumption and hence without a \(C\)-elbow.  The positive hard pair has \(e=b\) and \(d_e=d_b\), so the converse transfers to every larger Hu--Wager or cardinality-uniform stationary-overlap class containing this binary subclass.  For \(\zeta>0\) and \(C>1\), by contrast, the cited cardinality-uniform rate is \(T^{-1}+T^{-\beta}q_C^{2(1-\beta)}\), with \(\beta=2/(2+t_0\zeta)\), and its lower construction has \(2(Q+1)\) hidden states with \(Q\asymp\log T\), so that construction is not representable in the binary-hidden class for large \(T\).

items.label: Theorem T-3
items.nl:
Under the stationary-start, POMDP-kernel, sequential-assignment, and behavior-contraction assumptions, if \(e=b\), then \(P_e=P_b\), \(d_e=d_b\), and \(m_0=\theta\).  Moreover, the sample mean is unbiased and satisfies
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[\left\{T^{-1}\sum_{t=1}^{T}Y_t-\theta\right\}^2\right]
 \leq \frac{1+2/(1-\alpha)}{T}.
\]
Consequently its mean-squared error is \(O(T^{-1})\).  This is the standard on-policy reduction of the fixed-binary frontier; no law-by-law \(\Omega(T^{-1})\) assertion is made.

items.label: Theorem T-4
items.nl:
Let \(M:=\lceil(22+36/\alpha)T\rceil\) as in \(\mathrm{def{:}stable\text{-}grid\text{-}estimator}\). Before the Dobrushin filter is applied, its finite candidate list has exactly
\[
 \binom{M+3}{3}^{5}(M+1)^4
\]
elements, and filtering can only reduce this number. Hence, for fixed \(t_0>0\), the candidate-list cardinality is \(O(M^{19})=O(T^{19})\).

items.label: Cited result lem:cardinality-uniform-comparator
items.nl: For fixed \(t_0>0\) and \(\zeta>0\), the cardinality-uniform stationary-overlap POMDP result cited as \texttt{CausalSmithLatentOverlap2026} has minimax mean-squared-error rate \(T^{-1}+T^{-\beta}q_C^{2(1-\beta)}\), where \(\beta=2/(2+t_0\zeta)\) and \(q_C=(C-1)/C\).  Its lower-bound reset construction has \(2(Q+1)\) hidden states with \(Q\asymp\log T\).
